definition: The dissolved oragaanic carbon normalized absorbance at 254 nanometers. Can be related to dissolved organic matter aromaticity. Weishaar et al. 2003; doi: 10.1021/es030360x.
Spectral slope from 275-295 nanometers. Higher generally related with lower molecular weight dissolved organic matter (DOM). Helms et al. 2008; doi: 10.4319/lo.2008.53.3.0955.
R-squared for the spectral slope from 275 to 295 nanometers.
Spectral slope from 350-400 nanometers. Higher values generally indicated more aromatic; higher molecular weight dissolved organic matter (DOM). Helms et al. 2008; doi: 10.4319/lo.2008.53.3.0955.
R-squared for the spectral slope from 350 to 400 nanometers.
Spectral slope ratio. Defined as the ratio of S275_295/S350_400. Related to dissolved organic matter molecular weight. Helms et al. 2008;  doi: 10.4319/lo.2008.53.3.0955.
The ratio of absorption at 250 to 365 nanometers.
Fluorescence Index. Related to contribution of microbial (high) versus terrestrial sources (low). McKnight et al. 2001; doi: 10.4319/lo.2001.46.1.0038.
Humification Index. Related to the degree of humification. Ohno 2002; doi: 10.1021/es0155276.
Freshness Indices. Related to freshly produced dissolved organic matter. Parlanti et. al. 2000; doi: 10.1016/S0146-6380(00)00124-8.
Biological Index. Related to autotrophic activity (>1 value indicates recently generated dissolved organic matter (DOM)). Huguet et al. 2009; doi: 10.1016/j.orggeochem.2009.03.002.
